native_result.query: In which millenium did amber had the highest value and in what time interval did it peak?
native_result.HypoA: Amber has historically high and stable values in the 4th millenium BCE. with its all time peak around 3300 to 3000BCE.
native_result.HypoB: Amber reached its highest value in the 4th millennium BCE (4000–3001 BCE), peaking in the interval 3300–3000 BCE (CE −3300 to −3000; 5250–4950 calBP), where the amber Z-score plateaus at its series maximum of Z = +1.54 across four consecutive 100-year anchor points (3300, 3200, 3100, 3000 BCE), during the Middle Neolithic ('MN') period group. This peak crowns an already-elevated 4th millennium (second-highest plateau Z = +1.46 during 4000–3400 BCE; millennium mean Z = +1.484, the highest of any millennium), after which amber values collapse (Z ≤ +0.37 from 2900 BCE, mostly negative thereafter). Boundary caveat: the plateau's final anchor year, 3000 BCE, lies exactly on the 4th/3rd-millennium boundary; naive floor-binning yields a nominal max tie, resolved in favor of the 4th millennium BCE by bin means (+1.484 vs −0.148) and by the strict convention 4th millennium BCE = 4000–3001 BCE. The interpolated ≥1.0 envelope's early edge (CE −4018) is a linear-interpolation artifact and was not used as the peak start.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded all three files, verifying chronology consistency: time_series_data.csv CE ascending 1-yr steps with calBP = 1950 − CE exactly; capital.csv BCE positive and descending at 100-yr steps (comma-decimal quoted parsing); pollen file descending with the same calBP convention. 2) Cross-validated capital.csv Zamber against raw Amber in time_series_data.csv via CE = −BCE: identical at all 37 overlapping anchors (max abs diff 0.0). 3) Treated the 37 raw 100-year Amber anchors as ground truth; Amber_inter (fully populated, step interpolation) used only to confirm plateau continuity. 4) Descriptive statistics of Amber, Amber_inter, Zamber. 5) Identified the maximum (Z = 1.54) and its contiguous anchor interval (3300–3000 BCE), converted to CE and calBP. 6) Ranked BCE millennia by bin max and bin mean under the strict 4th-millennium-BCE = 4000–3001 BCE convention; performed a floor-binning sensitivity check showing the 3000-BCE boundary tie is resolved by bin means. 7) Documented the interpolated ≥1.0 envelope as context with an explicit interpolation-artifact caveat.
